rows.description: Kids say "you can't play with us". I feel a stone in my tummy and tears come. It is not because I am bad. Wise action: tell a teacher or find another game. A grown-up can help by making a place for me.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, compassion, indifference
paired view exists: Actor (S529)

rows.description: I say "no girls" or "no you" to feel powerful in my group. I do not yet understand how it hurts. A wise teacher helps me imagine how the child feels and to say "come and play". The harmful pattern is making it a group rule.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, compassion, indifference
paired view exists: Receiver (S528)
related mind states: hurt

rows.description: Nobody notices me on the playground and I stand alone. I feel invisible. A wise adult helps me practise a friendly line or plans a small play date. Loneliness at this age needs adult help, not shame.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, compassion, rejection
related mind states: shame, loneliness

rows.description: A child calls "come, you can be the goalkeeper!" I feel warm relief, as if I belong. I remember who invited me and try to invite others. Being welcomed teaches me to welcome the next child.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, indifference, rejection
related mind states: relief

rows.description: The teacher sees me alone and sits beside me, then invites others to join. I feel seen and less lonely. Wise adults help without embarrassing the child and without forcing others to like them.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, indifference, rejection
related mind states: embarrassment, loneliness, empathy

rows.description: A bigger child pushes me and takes my things and says "don't tell". I am scared. It is not my fault. Wise action: tell a parent or teacher even if I was told not to. Telling is safe, not tale-telling.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, contempt, loyalty, trust
related mind states: fear, trust

rows.description: A child mocks how I look or talk and others laugh. I feel small and hot-eyed. This is about the bully, not me. I can walk away and tell a trusted adult. Staying silent lets the hurt grow.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, fear, loyalty, trust
related mind states: amusement, contempt, trust, hurt

rows.description: I hit a child who teased me and now I am in trouble. I felt helpless and hitting seemed the only answer. Wiser: say "stop" loudly and get a teacher. Adults should also ask what made me so upset.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: contempt, fear, loyalty, trust
related mind states: anger

rows.description: I tell my teacher and she believes me and acts. I feel relief and safe. Being believed is the most important thing that happens after bullying, and I learn that speaking up works.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, contempt, fear, loyalty
related mind states: relief, trust

rows.description: I push smaller children and feel powerful. Underneath I may be sad or copying someone at home. I need firm limits and a warm adult to teach other ways of feeling strong. Only punishing does not fix it.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, contempt, fear, loyalty, trust
related mind states: sadness, hostility
